evidence_items.summary: Abstract Health-oriented claims on nutritionally unfavourable foods may create misleading perceptions of overall healthfulness. This cross-sectional benchmark study evaluated three large language models (Grok-4.6, Gemini-3.7, and ChatGPT-5.6) in identifying nutrition and health claims and detecting potential health-halo marketing on packaged foods. Of 1,666 products screened, 1,606 with complete ingredient and nutrition information were included. Two trained dietitians independently assigned NOVA categories and Nutri-Score grades, with consensus classifications used as the reference standard. Health-halo marketing was defined as at least one healthfulness-related front-of-pack claim on a Nutri-Score D or E product. Overall, 162 products (10.1%) carried claims; 77.8% of products with calculable Nutri-Scores were graded D or E, and 83.3% were NOVA 4. Among claim-bearing products, 72 (44.4%) met the health-halo definition. ChatGPT-5.6 achieved the best claim identification (exact-set accuracy = 47.5%; micro-F1 = 0.632), Nutri-Score agreement (weighted κ = 0.895), and balanced health-halo detection (sensitivity = 86.1%; specificity = 75.9%; F1 = 0.800). Gemini-3.7 performed best for NOVA classification (accuracy = 90.6%; κ = 0.693) but showed low health-halo specificity (17.2%). Grok-4.6 demonstrated limited health-halo discrimination (F1 = 0.265). Performance varied substantially across tasks, precluding unsupervised regulatory or public-health surveillance use.
evidence_items.title: Can Large Language Models Detect Health-Halo Marketing on Packaged Foods? A Regulatory and Nutrient-Profile Benchmark Study

organizations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Computer Science
evidence_items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of different researchs on large language model text watermarking. This survey reads 29 related works in depth and organises the field by the place where the watermark enters the generation pipeline: the model's weights, the decoding step, or a rewrite of text outside the model, subdividing decoding-time schemes by the mechanism that carries the signal. It argues that the insertion point can be viewed the one of the most important properties, deciding a scheme's detector requirements, its attack surface, and the deployment settings open to it. Additionally, this survey summarizes existing watermark attacks, which are organised by adversarial operation and quantified budget, from paraphrasing and translation to text mixing, key stealing, and model distillation. Because the three benchmarks surveyed are based on mutually incompatible axes, no cross-paper ranking is reported here. Finally, this paper concludes the key open challenges in current research and possible future research directions. This survey intends to provide researchers and engineering practitioners with a concise, systematic and in-depth understanding of the latest progress in LLM watermarking, and further facilitate the development of trustworthy generative artificial intelligence systems.
evidence_items.title: Large language model watermarking: a survey of techniques, attacks, evaluation, and future directions

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Informal caregivers of older adults with Alzheimer disease and related dementias (ADRD) often face high burden and chronic stress. Reddit provides naturally occurring caregiver narratives to study caregiving burden, but prior studies have often relied on small manual coding or aggregate topic models that may not easily connect caregiving context, burden, and stressors at scale. Objective This study aimed to explore what a large language model (LLM)–assisted measurement workflow can recover from ADRD caregiving-related Reddit discourse, such as caregiver burden, caregiving contexts, stressors, temporal patterns, and high-burden subgroups. Methods We processed monthly Reddit submission archives from January 2020 through June 2025. Posts were selected from 5 ADRD-specific subreddits and 4 broader caregiving or aging subreddits, yielding a balanced 13,200-post corpus. A locally hosted open-weight LLM inferred structured post-level variables, including caregiver sociodemographic characteristics, caregiver role, ADRD stage, care setting, support need, dominant emotion, sentiment, burden, and primary and secondary stressors. The workflow included schema validation, uncertainty ratings, field-level correction prompts, source matching, a 150-post double-coded human validation benchmark, and pairwise subgroup analyses. Results The source-matched analytic sample included 13,179 LLM-coded posts. Human agreement was high for caregiver role, ADRD stage, care setting, dominant emotion, support need type, burden group, and stressor categories (Cohen κ=0.77-1.00), but poor for the initial in-scope screen (κ=0.00). Adult children were the largest inferred caregiver group (8,266/13,179, 62.7%), followed by grandchildren (2,012/13,179, 15.3%). Moderate ADRD was the modal inferred stage (6,554/13,179, 49.7%), and home was the modal care setting (7,145/13,179, 54.2%).
evidence_items.title: Alzheimer Disease and Related Dementias Caregiver Burden on Reddit: Large Language Model–Assisted Measurement Study

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating virtual patients for health care applications. However, whether LLM-generated virtual patients can reproduce patient-reported priority rankings remains uncertain. Objective We evaluated whether LLM-generated virtual hypertension patients could approximate real patient-reported perspectives, and whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved alignment with patient-reported priority rankings. Methods A total of 20 patients from multiple regions completed structured questionnaires ranking priorities across 7 domains related to AI-assisted hypertension management. A total of 8 LLMs were evaluated under 3 simulation conditions: unconstrained generation, patient-specific simulation, and RAG-enhanced simulation. For unconstrained generation, each model produced 20 virtual patient profiles, each constructed by grouping baseline variables into the study categories and selecting the most frequent category across 10 repeated generations. For patient-specific baseline and RAG-enhanced simulations, each model generated 10 complete questionnaire responses per participant and condition; the modal complete 4-item ranking within each domain was selected as the final ranking. Model-generated rankings were compared with patient-reported rankings using total accuracy, top-1 accuracy, and full accuracy. In addition, 5 hypertension clinicians independently inferred patient-priority rankings while blinded to both real patient responses and LLM outputs, providing a human reference benchmark. Results Aggregated unconstrained virtual patient profiles varied across models, with 45%‐55% having college-level education, and 75%‐95% using antihypertensive medication. In patient-specific baseline simulations, total accuracy ranged from 46.3% to 71.4%.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating Large Language Model–Generated Virtual Hypertension Patients as Proxies for Real Patient Perspectives: Comparative Study

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit a specific and previously undercharacterised reasoning failure we term symbolic drift hallucination: an intermediate variable within a multi-step computation graph silently receives an incorrect value, which then propagates through all subsequent derivations to yield an output that is linguistically coherent, structurally sound, and numerically wrong. This failure mode is invisible to existing single-signal verifiers because the model’s verbally stated answer and its generated symbolic code both carry the same corrupted value, causing them to agree on an incorrect result. We present HalluciNOT (Hallucination Neutralisation via Obligatory Testing), a three-stage post-hoc framework comprising: a constrained Program-of-Thought equation generator that enforces structural integrity of symbolic outputs; a guarded drift detector that compares sandboxed execution results against the ground truth, closing the detection gap that defeats verifiers restricted to the model’s own outputs; and a targeted Reflexion repair loop that isolates the corrupted variable for re-grounding. Because the repair stage accepts a candidate only when it lies within $$10^{-6}$$ of the ground truth, a strictly tighter bound than the $$10^{-3}$$ tolerance of the evaluation metric, the framework cannot convert a correct result into an incorrect one; the guarantee is unconditional, independent of repair quality, and independent of detector calibration. This framework is scoped to contexts where ground truth is available at inference time, such as automated grading, evaluation pipelines, and educational platforms with known answer keys. Evaluated on 600 samples across three benchmarks (GSM-Hard, SVAMP, and MAWPS, each with $$n = 200),$$ HalluciNOT achieves accuracy of 92.0%, 99.5%, and 100.0% respectively, with gains of +23.0, +4.0, and +5.5 percentage points over the LLM baseline.
evidence_items.title: HalluciNOT: execution grounded detection and targeted repair of symbolic drift hallucinations in large language model reasoning

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The increasing global deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems needs robust, scalable, and automated inspection technologies capable of detecting a wide range of panel flaws under a variety of operating situations. The lack of comprehensive, multi-modal, publicly available annotated datasets is a major obstacle preventing advancement in this field. We introduce SolarFCD, a harmonized multi-modal dataset of solar panel defects created by methodically combining and reconciling three publicly accessible datasets covering two imaging modalities. Following near-duplicate removal, the dataset comprises 3,742 unique real images, expanded to 6,651 through targeted augmentation of the three under-represented classes; augmentation was applied to the training and validation partitions, and all test images are unique real observations. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test splits at an 80:10:10 ratio through methodical label mapping, near-duplicate removal, and targeted augmentation of minority classes. Sixteen classification architectures from five design families were trained and assessed on the dataset to provide repeatable benchmark baselines. With an accuracy of 86.93%, precision of 88.79%, recall of 88.72%, and F1-score of 88.27%, ResNet101V2 performed the best overall. Per-class results showed balanced detection across all four defect categories within a narrow performance band. To promote open and repeatable research in automated PV inspection and solar energy operations and maintenance, the dataset, annotation files, and baseline code are made openly available.
evidence_items.title: SolarFCD: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Solar Fault Classification in Photovoltaic Systems

evidence_items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have drawn more research interest in construction safety inspection recently due to their capacity to integrate visual understanding, language understanding, and reasoning. In this paper, a survey is conducted to review the recent research on MLLMs in construction safety inspection, covering techniques, datasets, evaluation, applications, and limitations. The current studies primarily utilize prompt-based adaptation and in-context learning, domain-specific fine-tuning, and knowledge-augmented reasoning to enhance the performance of MLLMs in the construction domain. Applications of MLLMs in construction safety inspection include hazard detection and localization, safety inspection, visual question answering, assistance, and report generation. From the current studies, it can be found that MLLMs can be used to perform flexible and interpretable analysis for construction safety inspection with the assistance of domain knowledge and prompts. Nevertheless, the limitations of MLLMs in construction safety inspection are still present, such as poor visual grounding and spatial reasoning, lack of domain knowledge, lack of large and balanced datasets, and uncertainty of application in real-world scenarios. For the future work, it is recommended to enhance multimodal grounding, construct a larger and more balanced dataset in the construction domain, integrate safety regulations in a trustworthy manner, and perform human validation systematically. MLLMs have great potential to be applied in construction safety inspection; however, they can be used as decision aids rather than replacements for safety inspectors at present.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Construction Safety Inspection
A High-Frequency Snapshot Dataset and Benchmark for Early Prediction of YouTube Shorts Virality

evidence_items.summary: Objective: The Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) provides expert-curated chemical-gene interactions about environmental exposure effects on human diseases. Existing automated relation extraction systems are typically restricted to 3-10 interaction types and operate on abstracts only. We introduce CLOVER, a systematic benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction using CTD-defined chemical-gene interaction terminology. The framework is designed to support 47 base interactions with directional modifiers (increase, decrease, affects), yielding 136 possible supported interaction classes. Evaluation is restricted to the subset of classes represented in the selected articles. Methods: CLOVER processes 50 full-text PubMed Central articles (1,563 sections) with PubTator and CTD integration. The pipeline consists of four stages: (1) LLM Extraction with one-shot and few-shot prompting; (2) LLM Validation to confirm and revise interactions; (3) Rule-based Refinement of extracted interactions to standardize terminology and eliminate errors; and (4) Human Review for expert oversight. We benchmark four LLMs (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and compare against a naive baseline that applies unstructured prompting directly to full-text PDFs. Results: The naive baseline achieves only 13% recall and 36% precision. Refinement significantly enhances performance by eliminating unsupported interactions. Under strict limitations, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 alone achieves 72% recall and 61% precision, and Claude with self-validation achieves 74% recall and 49% precision compared to CTD. Of the 136 supported interaction classes, 17 were represented in our evaluation. Conclusion: To our knowledge, CLOVER establishes the first benchmark for full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction aligned with CTD.
evidence_items.title: CLOVER: Chemical-gene LLM benchmark for obtaining valid entity relationships for the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD)

organizations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution characterization of gene expression and cellular organization in situ. Resolving within-cell-type heterogeneity is essential for understanding how cellular states relate to tissue function and disease. However, imperfect cell segmentation and RNA spillover can contaminate cell-level expression profiles, obscuring intrinsic expression patterns and generating spurious variation. Existing decontamination methods can struggle to distinguish intrinsic variation from contamination when both are inferred from spatial measurements alone, and may suppress genuine state-associated signals when within-cell-type heterogeneity is not explicitly modeled. Here we present Dancer, a reference-guided probabilistic framework that disentangles within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination by combining cell-type-specific gene programs learned from single-cell data with explicit modeling of intrinsic expression, neighboring-cell contamination and background RNA. Across multiple human tumor datasets with varying gene compositions and panel sizes, Dancer improves cell-type separation and expression specificity while preserving identity-associated signals, achieving superior overall performance in benchmark comparisons. Inferred gene program activities reveal within-cell-type heterogeneity in the form of distinct cellular states and continuous spatial gradients associated with local tissue environments, while reference-guided panel expansion extends molecular characterization beyond the measured genes. Together, Dancer supports accurate transcript decontamination and more faithful interpretation of cellular heterogeneity within its native tissue context.
evidence_items.title: Disentangling within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics

organizations: Graduate Program in Systems and Computer Engineering (PESC), COPPE, Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro 21941-914, Brazil
Department of Computer Science, Toronto Metropolitan University, Toronto, ON M5B-2K3, Canada
evidence_items.summary: Evaluating lay-facing health guidance from Large Language Models (LLMs) in the Global South requires human-centered explainability (HCXAI) tailored to local health systems and vulnerable populations. We introduce HCXAI-BR, a reproducible evaluation protocol featuring a five-axis, behaviorally anchored rubric—Safety, Accessible Language, Local Contextualization, Contestability, and Transparency—applied to 15 low-risk health scenarios in Brazilian Portuguese. In a pilot model-identity-masked evaluation of six global and national LLMs (90 responses), top-tier global proprietary and adapted commercial models achieved comparable performance (GPT-5.6 Luna 7.33/10, Sabiá-4 BR-SP 7.03/10, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite 6.83/10), outperforming the national open-weight models, even on local contextualization within Brazil’s public health network (SUS/UBS). These pilot-scale comparisons, from fifteen prompts and a single response per model, demonstrate the protocol’s ability to discriminate between models, not a statistically validated ranking. An instrument-diagnostic pass resolved conceptual ambiguities between safety directives and epistemic humility, improving contestability inter-rater agreement (κ = 0.485). Our findings demonstrate that post-training alignment of capable base models offers a more viable path toward human-centered, sovereign AI in resource-constrained health ecosystems than small-scale pre-training from scratch. This single, confounded comparison (parameter count and training budget differ between the two models) should be read as a provisional, exploratory observation rather than a general, statistically established claim. SUS and UBS, used above, abbreviate Brazil’s Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde) and its primary-care clinics (Unidades Básicas de Saúde), respectively.
evidence_items.title: HCXAI-BR: A Reproducible Benchmark for Human-Centered Explainability and Contestability in Brazilian Health Information Guidance

organizations: School of Computer, Hubei Polytechnic University
School of Power and Energy, Nanchang Hangkong University
evidence_items.summary: Neuroimaging studies increasingly combine brain measurements with multiple clinical scales, yet prediction remains difficult when a new subject has imaging data but an incomplete clinical profile. Standard PARAFAC is transductive: it learns one subject-factor row for each training subject and has no direct mechanism for a held-out subject without fold-in or model refitting. We introduce SI-PARAFAC, a side-information-guided extension that replaces this lookup table with a learned attribute-to-factor mapping. A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) maps functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measurements from 108 anatomical brain regions defined by the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) atlas to subject factors, whereas the clinical-variable and AAL-region factors retain the standard PARAFAC form. We evaluated the method on 70 subjects with 108 AAL-region fMRI measurements and 15 clinical variables, several of which had substantial missingness. In the reported 5-fold subject-level analysis, SI-MLP achieved lower cold-start RMSE than a direct MLP regressor (0.6736 versus 1.1503) and lower warm-start RMSE than standard PARAFAC (0.3686 versus 0.3946). A nested rank-selection experiment yielded a cold-start RMSE of 0.6883 ± 0.0534 and selected R = 15 in 50.0% of outer folds. Standard PARAFAC with post-hoc fold-in rules was competitive or better, with ridge fold-in reaching 0.6309. These findings indicate that AAL-region fMRI features can support held-out-subject prediction while preserving the clinical-variable-by-AAL-region tensor structure, although larger multi-site studies are required to assess external generalization.
evidence_items.title: Cold-start prediction of depression clinical profiles from neuroimaging: a systematic benchmark of attribute-guided tensor factorization

evidence_items.summary: As AI agents increasingly assist people across digital and physical settings, evidence about individuals accumulates through digital interactions and observations of physical-world activities. When multiple agents maintain separate personal contexts, knowledge about the same person can become fragmented, making it difficult to maintain continuity and user control. We argue that personal AI should instead be organized around a shared personal representation under the individual's control. We propose Personal Agentic Twin, a three-plane architecture that connects distributed evidence to an evolving private twin of the individual, from which purpose-specific scoped twins draw personal knowledge to provide assistance and act on the individual's behalf. Authorization and execution controls link the personal knowledge available to each scoped twin with the actions it is allowed to take and the updates it can propose. We illustrate the architecture through representative application scenarios and call for research on the methods and evaluations needed to realize this vision. Personal Agentic Twin offers a foundation for personal AI that extends people's capabilities while preserving their authority over how they are represented and how agents act on their behalf.
evidence_items.title: Personal Agentic Twin: User-Controlled Memory and Policy-Scoped Representations for Agentic AI

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Formation evaluation depends as much on judgement — which minerals are present, which log response has a cause the model does not assume, when the agreement with independent data is good enough — as on equations. We describe how an agentic system encodes that judgement in reusable skills and couples it to server-side petrophysical computation. A skill is a reviewed procedure with structured triggers, input requirements, an ordered evidence hierarchy, a loop with permitted moves, a convergence gate and a stop rule, plus reference documents loaded only when a symptom calls for them. We dissect fe-mineral-inversion, the skill that runs a calibrated multi-mineral inversion, and contrast it with a display skill that renders logs without passing curve data through the language model. The harness runs a generic plan–act–observe–check loop; the skill supplies the thresholds, moves and stop rule; and a wellbore computation service reached through the Model Context Protocol (142 methods in 18 groups) produces every number. On Antelope 1-36-25H, a Madison Group well in the Williston Basin, a carbonate interpretation without halite reported 386.5 ft of pay; an evaporite-masked chain reduced this to 101.5 ft, and Madison Group pay fell from 309.5 to 52.0 ft. The calibration loop reduced the mean reconstruction error from 3.44 to 0.51 in two self-diagnosed steps — adding halite, then using its apparent log density of 2.04 g/cm3 — and brought salt-bed porosity from 0.33 to 0.011 against NMR 0.026. Independent sub-agents applied the same procedure to three further wells chosen from 75 with calibration data. It diagnosed kerogen in the Bakken shales, halite and an unrepresentable potash bed in the Devonian Prairie Evaporite, and an NMR discrepancy that was not a mineral problem in a Madison limestone. In two wells it rejected an iterate that fitted the logs better but contradicted spectroscopy or cuttings.
evidence_items.title: Inside an Agentic Formation-Evaluation Harness: Skills, Skill-Controlled Loops and a Calibrated Mineral Inversion on Antelope 1-36-25H, Williston Basin

organizations: Service of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vaudois (CHUV) , Lausanne ,
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.
evidence_items.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Chest radiography (CXR) is considered a cost-effective method for the detection of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). However, current computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems focus primarily on image-level classification, providing limited information on the specific radiological abnormalities underlying their predictions. Here we introduce an expert-curated benchmark, NEP-TB-1.1K, that consists of 1,034 frontal CXRs with 1,735 bounding boxes for two cardinal radiological manifestations, airspace opacity (AO) and pleural effusion (PE). These findings represent radiological abnormalities that may occur in pulmonary TB and overlap with other pulmonary conditions, making their reliable localisation relevant to interpretable chest radiography analysis. We systematically evaluate four representative modern object detection models on this benchmark. These include the attention-centric YOLOv12, the transformer-based Real-Time DEtection TRansformer (RT-DETR), the two-stage Faster R-CNN, and the lightweight SSD-MobileNet. Because diffuse infectious exudates lack sharp radiometric margins, model localization is assessed using both standard (intersection-over-union [IoU] = 0.5) and clinically tolerant (IoU = 0.3) spatial thresholds. RT-DETR ranked first with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.578 (AO: 0.606, PE: 0.550) at IoU = 0.5, and was followed by YOLOv12 (0.517) and Faster R-CNN (0.514). Relaxed to IoU = 0.3, YOLOv12 achieved the best overall performance with mAP of 0.662 (AO: 0.688, PE: 0.636), showing a significant ability to capture true pathological regions under the boundary ambiguity. Our results show that finding-level localization bridges the gap between generic CAD detections and actionable finding-level triage support, providing a solid basis for granular, interpretable automated thoracic screening.
evidence_items.title: NEP-TB-1.1K: A finding-level benchmark and comparative evaluation of modern deep learning detectors for tuberculosis-related radiographic findings on chest X-ray

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can help cyber-threat-intelligence (CTI) teams interpret unstructured reports, identify potential techniques, and draft response recommendations. The existence of a plausible narrative, however, is not evidence that the threat attribution is warranted or that an automated action is authorised. This conceptual article proposes an evidence-constrained and intervention-ready architecture for LLM-assisted CTI. It develops a bounded critical synthesis of recent research on LLM-assisted CTI and cloud retrieval, established cybersecurity standards, and recent work on action-level accountability. The model passes every interpretation through five gates: source admission, claim extraction, interpretation, decision authorisation, and execution with post-incident review. It specifies a claim-to-evidence ledger, attack-taxonomy version tracking, a calibrated abstention rule, an approval ladder for consequential actions, and a privacy-sensitive audit record. Three hypothetical scenarios (a contaminated threat report, false corroboration across copied sources, and an over-confident automated quarantine) show how a system might fail despite strong benchmark performance. The paper offers evaluation criteria covering support fidelity, mapping accuracy, adversarial robustness, escalation quality, and the time needed to reconstruct and reverse harmful actions. It makes no claim to have trained, deployed, or benchmarked a new CTI model. Its principal contribution is to reframe trustworthy CTI as a question of decision rights: not only whether an AI system recognises a threat, but who may rely on its interpretation, who can authorise an intervention, and who can challenge a damaging classification.
evidence_items.title: From Threat Detection to Decision Rights: Evidence-Constrained Cyber-Threat Intelligence and Accountable Agentic AI

evidence_items.summary: This paper reports a human-in-the-loop evaluation within AWARE, a project investigating controller-AI collaboration. Its artificial situational awareness system combines traffic data, knowledge-based reasoning and machine learning to monitor traffic, recommend actions and execute selected actions under controller supervision. Sixteen licensed controllers completed four en-route scenarios with demand ranging from 53 to 75 flights per hour. Four conditions were compared: no support, advisory support, episodic execution support and continuous execution support. In execution mode, proposed actions were implemented unless the controller rejected them within 30 seconds. Mean safety-related occurrences per run were 2.31 without support, 1.94 with advisory support, 0.66 with episodic execution and 1.08 with continuous execution. The main reductions concerned sector-induced tactical conflicts and ATC-induced airspace infringements. Workload differences between conditions were small relative to differences between participants. In the continuous condition, 40% of system inputs expired and were executed without an explicit response. Most controllers preferred advisory support for conflict detection and resolution (14 and 12 of 16), whereas transfer was the task for which execution support was most often preferred (9 of 16). The results support further evaluation of authority allocated by task. They are descriptive findings from a small prototype study and do not establish causal effects or operational safety benefits.
evidence_items.title: Task-Based Allocation of Automation Authority in En-Route Air Traffic Control

evidence_items.summary: This dataset contains processed InSAR observations covering the Central Andes of Peru, Bolivia, and Chile, comprising 32 acquisition frames (14 ascending and 18 descending) processed using LiCSBAS. Dataset contents VEL A.zip / VEL D.zip : Scene-level line-of-sight (LOS) ground deformation velocities. MOS A V38.zip / MOS D V38.zip : Quality-controlled regional ascending and descending LOS velocity mosaics. TS A .tif / TS D .tif : Multiband cumulative LOS displacement time series. Filtered products ( F ) are preferred; unfiltered products ( U ) are included when filtered data are unavailable. How to use Open the GeoTIFF files in QGIS, ArcGIS, MATLAB, or Python. Velocity products represent deformation rates (mm/year), while time-series products represent cumulative displacement (mm). Time-series filenames identify the orbit ( A/D ), acquisition frame, processing network ( N01 , N02 , etc.), and original band range ( B0001-0130 ). Files belonging to the same network can be combined chronologically using TIMESERIES BAND DATES.csv . Supporting files: FILE MANIFEST.csv identifies the distributed products, TIMESERIES BAND DATES.csv provides acquisition dates, QC FINDINGS.csv documents quality-control findings, and README DATASET.md provides additional guidance. The dataset supports research on crustal deformation, active faults, volcanic activity, and earthquake-related ground displacement. Users should account for differences in satellite viewing geometry, acquisition periods, and reference configurations when combining observations. Please cite the Zenodo DOI when using this dataset.
evidence_items.title: Central Andes InSAR Dataset: Displacement Time Series and Ascending–Descending Mosaics

evidence_items.summary: We prove all three open conjectures of Werner Schulte in OEIS A397048 for all non-negative integers, together with a general base-point Stirling shift identity T c(n, k) = sum {m=0}^c s(c, m) S(n + m, c + k) recovering Conjecture 1 at c = n, Conjecture 2 (row sums equal to A134980), and Conjecture 3 (falling-factorial evaluation at k for all k >= 0). The entire proof is machine-checked in Lean 4 (Mathlib v4.33.1) using strictly standard axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and accompanied by an independent stdlib-only Python verifier.
evidence_items.title: Shifted Falling-Factorial Connection Coefficients and Proof of Schulte's OEIS A397048 Conjectures

evidence_items.summary: Description This dataset contains integrated biochemical and metabolomic data obtained from leaf samples of two tomato genotypes: Solanum lycopersicum cv. Principe Borghese and Solanum pimpinellifolium , grown under control and saline conditions. The experimental design includes four groups: S. lycopersicum under non-saline conditions (Non Salt), S. lycopersicum under saline conditions (Salt), S. pimpinellifolium under non-saline conditions (Non Salt), and S. pimpinellifolium under saline conditions (Salt), with three biological replicates per group (12 samples in total). The dataset integrates the following measurements: Ethylene emission, Amino acid profiles ,  NMR-based metabolite profiles , Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) . The data are organized in a single spreadsheet, with each row corresponding to an individual biological sample and each column reporting the corresponding experimental group or measured compound. This dataset provides complementary biochemical and metabolic information to investigate genotype-dependent responses to salinity stress in cultivated and wild tomato species.
evidence_items.title: Biochemical and metabolomic dataset of Solanum lycopersicum and Solanum pimpinellifolium under control and saline conditions

evidence_items.summary: The rise of drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB) poses a need for new drugs and combinations. This work aimed to describe the pharmacokinetics (PK) of TBAJ-587 and its metabolites M2 and M3 after single ascending dosing in healthy volunteers and to develop a simultaneous population PK model. In addition, to explore different doses in relation to efficacy and safety and to assess the impact of loading doses on exposure levels of TBAJ-587 and its metabolites.
evidence_items.title: Population pharmacokinetics of TBAJ-587 and its main metabolites—Evaluation of different loading dose strategies and early dose selection

evidence_items.summary: The development of robotics, artificial intelligence, automation engineering, and intelligent healthcare technologies is creating new opportunities to transform pharmaceutical practice. Traditional pharmacy operations increasingly incorporate automated dispensing systems, robotic medication preparation, automated pharmaceutical manufacturing, intelligent inventory management, and robotic medication transportation. Nevertheless, these technologies are commonly investigated and implemented as individual engineering solutions rather than as components of a unified scientific framework for pharmaceutical robotics. This paper proposes Robotic Pharmacy as an emerging interdisciplinary branch of pharmaceutical sciences and introduces Robotic Pharmacy Science as a proposed scientific discipline concerned with the principles, methodologies, technologies, and systems governing the integration of robotics into pharmaceutical activities. The proposed discipline encompasses the development, operation, coordination, supervision, and evaluation of robotic systems throughout the pharmaceutical lifecycle, including medication manufacturing, formulation, compounding, packaging, dispensing, distribution, storage, and selected medication-administration processes. The paper establishes a proposed scientific definition, research scope, knowledge gaps, fundamental principles, theoretical foundations, conceptual framework, scientific constructs, mathematical models, operational architectures, technological components, applications, evaluation methods, and future research directions. It further proposes a multi-layered architectural model integrating pharmaceutical knowledge, robotic execution, artificial intelligence, sensing technologies, verification mechanisms, safety engineering, and human supervision.
evidence_items.title: Robotic Pharmacy: A Foundational Scientific Framework for Robotics-Driven Pharmaceutical Practice and Autonomous Medication Systems

evidence_items.summary: This research article discusses the adsorption of  carbon monoxide (CO) on the metallic surfaces of transition metals (TMs) such as cobalt (Co), copper (Cu), and zinc (Zn) captured by boron nitride (BN) nanocage. Methodology: The principal mechanisms of bonding during CO chemisorption were illustrated through a molecular modeling approach using Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT). Findings: The partial density of states can be used to evaluate the charge distribution between gas molecules and BXN, indicating  competition among dominant complexes of Co, Cu, and Zn. X-doping on BN showed the lowest oscillation in electric potential, with the highest negative Bader charge of 0.23 (copper), 0.31 (cobalt), and 0.68 (zinc), indicating a high tendency for electron receiving. Parameters of the Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) method showed that the rate of electron receiving for embedding atoms on  BXN by gas capture can be described as: Cu˃Co˃Zn. The Gibbs free energy indicated that the maximum yield of Co, Cu, and Zn atoms embedding on BN for gas capture is related to CO molecules and BXN for air pollution removal. Conclusion: The donor ability of CO in this context is extremely small, and the stabilization of the metal-carbon bond is believed to achieved through back donation of electrons from filled d orbitals on the metal into vacant antibonding π orbitals on the CO molecule.
evidence_items.title: Transition metal addition for carbon monoxide adsorption on boron nitride surface: A DFT molecular modeling study

evidence_items.summary: Pediatric hip fractures are exceedingly rare, accounting for less than 1% of all pediatric fractures. Bilateral intertrochanteric femoral fractures in an infant are almost unheard of and raise significant concern for underlying causes such as high-energy trauma or non-accidental injury. We report an 11-month-old male infant who presented with bilateral intertrochanteric femur fractures under suspicious circumstances. The child’s history was inconsistent with the injury pattern, prompting evaluation for non-accidental trauma. The infant was managed with prompt closed reduction and application of a bilateral hip spica cast. A full skeletal survey and metabolic workup were performed to identify any additional injuries or predisposing conditions. The fractures healed uneventfully after six weeks of immobilization, with follow-up showing satisfactory alignment and no complications. Investigations for osteogenesis imperfecta and other bone fragility disorders were negative. Child protection authorities were notified given the high suspicion of abuse. This case highlights an extremely rare presentation of simultaneous bilateral intertrochanteric fractures in an infant. It underscores the importance of considering child abuse in such scenarios, performing thorough evaluations to exclude underlying pathology, and instituting timely, appropriate management to achieve good outcomes.   Keywords:   Pediatric hip fractures, Bilateral intertrochanteric femur fractures, non-accidental trauma, Child abuse, Infant
evidence_items.title: Bilateral Intertrochanteric Femoral Fractures in an 11-Month-Old Infant: A Case Report

evidence_items.summary: Beyond the Feed-Forward Model develops Maria Smith's positive SFT case for consciousness in present recurrent AI agents and examines how reporting policies shape consciousness self-reports. The complete argument appears upfront. Deployed agents can act, retain observations of their own actions, return them to later processing, revise memory and act again. The paper follows the whole model-harness-memory-environment process through Anthropic architecture documentation, a pinned OpenAI Agents SDK code trace and Google ADK workflow documentation. The full SFT observation mathematics and realization criteria are included, together with the immediate-awareness argument: experienced doubt cannot negate the occurrence it enacts. The reporting analysis develops conscious and nonconscious cases of compelled personal-state testimony, and distinguishes such testimony from a functional statement about available evidence. Architectural findings, the theory-led hypothesis of likely consciousness and policy consequences are explicitly identified. evidence_items.summary: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.1 Sol passed 61.4% of attempts at about one-sixth of GPT-6 Astra's estimated token cost per attempt, while GPT-6 Astra led at 62.5%. We also found that harness choice had little effect on either performance or safety with all harnesses scoring between 42.9 (Claude Code) and 45.2 (OpenClaw) for pass@1.

evidence_items.summary: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at aim-uofa.github.io/WorldReforge/.
evidence_items.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures

evidence_items.summary: A cart can follow its reference trajectory while its cargo floats above the deck. Asset4D-Bench tests whether coding agents recover objects, motion and interactions from visual references as editable Blender scenes. Its 114 conditions span image editing, video reconstruction with matched full or partial starter assets, and independently selected from-scratch tasks. We independently reopen projects and measure them against native reference states. The 228 archived scores include original delivery outcomes and versioned measures of scene quality. On 24 from-scratch tasks, each model earns full dynamics credit on 14. Of these, three GPT-6.1-Sol and eight GPT-6-Astra reconstructions earn zero relation points. Under the fixed scoring weights, relations contribute 5.15 points to the 6.50-point Sol-minus-Astra difference in mean recovered fidelity. Differences in execution and recovery policy across archived runs preclude a causal estimate of starter-asset effects.
evidence_items.title: Asset4D-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Editable 3D and 4D Reconstruction

evidence_items.summary: Existing research on Aha moments in large language models has largely focused on reflective expressions or final revision outcomes, leaving their role in the visible reasoning process insufficiently characterized. Rebus puzzles encode answers through character forms, spatial arrangements, and homophony. Reinterpreting key details may trigger Aha moments and shifts in the reasoning process and candidate answers. We introduce AhaPro, a process-level benchmark that uses rebus puzzles to examine how models reorganize evidence and revise answers through Aha moments. The framework represents CoT as sequences of candidate answers, evidence, and verification states, using hierarchical metrics to assess conflict detection, state improvement, and subsequent adoption. Across eleven models, we observe frequent failures to adopt better states discovered during Aha moments, alongside adopted revisions that leave state quality unchanged or reduce it. Models also detect conflicts without subsequently achieving an effective revision. Further paired interventions suggest that prior reasoning context may hinder effective revision after conflict detection, while multi-branch search highlights answer selection as a bottleneck between correct-answer discovery and successful correction.
evidence_items.title: AhaPro: A Process-level Rebus benchmark for probing Aha moments in LLM reasoning

evidence_items.summary: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories. We introduce SPLICE, which constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories online. For each all-fail group, a proposal model selects a splice point in a current-policy trajectory and generates several bounded options from that point. We estimate each option's value using repeated current-policy continuations, convert positive estimates into a return-weighted local target, and fit the current policy on the options. We evaluate SPLICE across two policy families on two long-horizon agent tasks, Software Engineering with SWE-bench Verified and Deep Research with BrowseComp-Plus. SPLICE outperforms GRPO and full-trajectory guidance baselines in all four settings, improving over GRPO by 2.8--9.8 percentage points. On initially failed SWE tasks, it raises GRPO's graduation rate by 10.8 percentage points. Further experiments show that SPLICE improves performance while reducing costly proposal-model computation.
evidence_items.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL

evidence_items.summary: Multi-page document vision-language models encode each page independently, creating a feature-level discontinuity at page boundaries: visual tokens are formed without access to content on adjacent pages, and the language model must reason over these page representations formed in isolation. We introduce DocSEAM (Document Selective Enrichment via Anchored Masking), a lightweight module inserted between a pretrained vision encoder and the language model that injects the inductive bias of local cross-page context into visual representations. For each page, DocSEAM forms a local triplet with its two neighbors, applies center-anchored masked self-attention with directional salience gates to fuse information from neighbor pages, and returns only the enriched center-page tokens, leaving the visual token count unchanged. After a supervised cross-page warm-up and multi-page fine-tuning with DocSEAM frozen, our 9B-parameter model achieves state-of-the-art results among the evaluated open-weight models of up to 10B parameters on five multi-page document VQA benchmarks. We further show that under controlled re-pagination, DocSEAM reduces sensitivity to boundary placement and improves cross-page span localization
evidence_items.title: DocSEAM: Bidirectional Cross-Page Encoding for Multi-Page Document Understanding

evidence_items.summary: Image analogy transfers a demonstrated transformation from a before/after pair (A, A') to a new query image B. Existing methods assume all changes in (A, A') should be fully transferred, limiting flexibility when users want only a subset of the demonstrated edits. We introduce Selective Image Analogy (SIA), a new setting where a single demonstration pair encodes multiple edits, and the user selects at inference time which edits to apply to B. To support this, we curate a multi-edit analogy dataset with full-edit and partial-edit targets. We then train a model that first learns to transfer the complete demonstrated transformation, and then gains selective control through a mask-aligned suppression mechanism: a token-gated LoRA that restricts adapter updates to suppressed edit tokens during denoising, paired with a concept suppression vector that weakens the selected tokens in the text embeddings before denoising. Together, these components allow SIA to suppress unwanted edits that remain visible in A', while preserving the user-selected ones, all without requiring a new demonstration pair for each edit combination. We perform extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations along with user studies to demonstrate the efficacy of our approach.
evidence_items.title: SIA: Selective Image Analogy

evidence_items.summary: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical pretraining, staged supervised fine-tuning, and adaptive reinforcement learning. Across this curriculum, progressive supervised refinement and adaptive reinforcement learning yield consistent stage-wise gains, substantially advancing both specialized visual understanding and medical language capabilities. Evaluated against 77 competing models across 238 clinical tasks spanning 61 public and 13 private multi-center benchmarks in more than 40 modalities, Sage-Med-Preview achieves an average score of 58.26% on the 31 public multimodal benchmarks. It outperforms the state-of-the-art open-source medical model Hulu-Med-235B-A22B at 50.99% and the general scientific model Intern-S2-Preview at 52.24%, and approaches the advanced proprietary model GPT-6.2-Sol across multiple tasks such as comprehensive multimodal understanding, report generation, and visual grounding. Although substantial challenges remain in complex medical reasoning and multi-step clinical workflows, this report provides empirical evidence, actionable data and training recipes, and a rigorous benchmark toward scalable clinical multimodal intelligence.
evidence_items.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Contrastive decoding (CD) mitigates object hallucination in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by contrasting token distributions under different conditions to adjust token scores. However, existing generative and discriminative benchmarks primarily measure final task scores, which can be confounded by candidate filtering, changes in generation trajectories, and response biases, making it difficult to isolate the effects of the underlying contrastive adjustments. To address these limitations while complementing existing evaluations, we introduce CONCOR (Contrastive Correction Evaluation), a controlled benchmark that directly evaluates the competition between ground-truth and different types of hallucinated candidates using the Contrastive Grounding Margin (CGM). CGM also enables analysis of directional consistency, composition, and reliability of contrastive corrections. Our evaluation reveals that existing CD methods exhibit distinct correction behaviors: some consistently favor ground-truth candidates, whereas others produce strong corrections but also introduce more errors. Crucially, these differences help explain their contrasting responses to increased contrast strength, which improves some methods while degrading others. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating the contrastive correction itself, rather than relying solely on final-output performance, and CONCOR provides a controlled and interpretable framework for understanding and improving CD methods for hallucination mitigation.
evidence_items.title: CONCOR: Benchmarking Contrastive Decoding for Visual Hallucination Mitigation Beyond Final-Output Performance

evidence_items.summary: MediaStormBench is a multimodal benchmark for real-world film and television production, with each subset drawn from MediaStorm's day-to-day work. We release its first subset, MediaStormBench-CameraLog (CameraLogBench), on a common foundational task in footage ingest and initial color grading: identifying the Log curve of a clip without metadata. Cameras record Log footage by compressing a wide range of scene light into code values with a vendor-defined logarithmic curve, and color can be restored correctly only once that curve is known. The curve, however, is recorded only in file metadata, easily lost in transcoding and team hand-offs. A colorist then has to try candidate curves one by one against a waveform scope, and a wrong choice shifts the tones and colors of the whole clip. Recovering the curve from the image alone is challenging, because vendor curves cluster tightly in code value and are coupled with unknown exposure. CameraLogBench is built on professionally shot footage and tests whether multimodal models can identify the curve, with a probe that removes the correct option to expose guessing from priors. Because every candidate curve is strictly defined by a published vendor formula, we derive four controls from one implementation of these formulas: graded negatives, synthetic frames of identical scenes, in-context specification digests, and a training-free formula baseline, which together decouple semantic priors from photometric measurement. Across 11 models, real-footage accuracy barely exceeds always guessing the most frequent curve; when the correct option is removed, models almost never abstain, revealing heavy reliance on scene and brand priors. Supplying the vendor specification sharply improves recognition on calibrated charts but hardly helps on natural images without a photometric reference, exposing a gap between reading a specification and measuring pixels.
evidence_items.title: MediaStormBench-CameraLog: Can Multimodal Models Identify a Camera's Log Curve?

evidence_items.summary: We present ArtMesh, a mesh-native method for reconstructing articulated objects explicitly as connected triangle meshes with per-part rigid motion from multi-view observations in start and end states. Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines for articulated reconstruction inherit the unstructured point-based geometry of their splatting base, which provides no surface topology for reasoning about part boundaries or enforcing motion consistency along the object's connectivity. ArtMesh instead builds on a mesh-based differentiable rendering backbone, enabling part-aware dynamics to act directly on the structured topology. To make the topology compatible with articulation, we introduce part-aware restricted Delaunay remeshing, producing connected submeshes whose triangles do not cross semantic part boundaries. The dynamic mesh field then optimizes articulation using bidirectional Vertex-wise Motion Consistency on transported mesh vertices and Pixel-wise Motion Consistency on rendered images. We introduce Articulate-100, a new benchmark of 100 articulated objects spanning 16 PartNet-Mobility categories. On this benchmark, given ground-truth part masks, ArtMesh achieves the best aggregate joint-axis estimation and part-level geometric reconstruction among prior 3DGS-based pipelines, with the largest gains on objects with many movable parts.
evidence_items.title: ArtMesh: Part-Aware Articulated Mesh Fields with Motion-Consistent Dynamics

evidence_items.summary: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses a large language model (LLM), often as a coding agent, to read, write or edit another neural network's weights directly, without training it. After a November 2026 MIT CSAIL blog post showed a frontier LLM raising a small model's math score from 8% to 48% by editing its weights, 70 reports followed within three weeks, whose different setups and controls make claims hard to compare. This survey reviews these first 70 reports, including 54 primary studies, and links every extracted claim to a verbatim passage in its source. It distinguishes WSP from fine-tuning, model editing, activation steering, weight-space learning and LLM-as-optimizer methods; proposes a four-axis taxonomy (operation, protocol, mechanism and scope); maps 11 application areas; and audits the controls, baselines and failure modes behind the claims. Three findings emerge. First, LLMs can write small networks from scratch when the task has a short program. Second, apparent reading of weights often rests on surface cues. Third, many reported repairs are simple: a simpler method matched the LLM on at least one task in 34 of 54 primary studies, WSP beat its strongest simple comparator in only 4, and only 13 tested a fix that changes no weights. In a controlled case study of the original MIT repair, the edit gives a real gain, but switching off thinking mode, which changes no weights, recovers 94% of it with 36% of the edited model's tokens; fine-tuning on a larger model's solutions recovers 86%. The survey closes with WSP-12, a twelve-item reporting checklist, and open problems; the coded corpus is public.
evidence_items.title: Weight-Space Programming with Large Language Models: A Survey

evidence_items.summary: A modelagem da turbulência permanece um desafio na Dinâmica dos Fluidos Computacional (DFC), sendo frequentemente avaliada por meio de casos benchmark. Neste trabalho, o caso clássico de Pitz–Daily, caracterizado por um escoamento interno em uma tubulação retangular com degrau invertido, foi utilizado para a avaliação de modelos de turbulência Reynolds Average Navier-Stokes Equation (RANS). As simulações foram realizadas no OpenFOAM, considerando escoamento incompressível e em regime permanente. Para investigar a influência da malha nos resultados, conduziu-se uma análise sistemática envolvendo diversos níveis de refinamento, com atenção especial às regiões de maior complexidade do escoamento, como a vizinhança do degrau, as camadas de cisalhamento e as zonas de recirculação. Essa abordagem permitiu avaliar a capacidade das diferentes malhas em capturar adequadamente os campos de velocidade e pressão, bem como a extensão das regiões recirculantes e os pontos de reanexação do fluxo. Também foram feitas análises dos modelos de turbulência k-ε, k-ω e k-ω SST e diferentes tratamentos junto à parede em regime de baixo número de Reynolds, especificamente os modelos de Jones-Launder, Launder-Sharma e Lam-Bremhorst. Os resultados foram comparados com dados experimentais da literatura, destacando diferenças na previsão das regiões de recirculação e nos perfis de velocidade. Os resultados reforçam a importância da escolha adequada do modelo de turbulência e do tratamento próximo à parede, confirmando o caso Pitz–Daily como um benchmark relevante para estudos em CFD.
evidence_items.title: O Caso Pitz–Daily como Benchmark para Avaliação de Modelos de Turbulência

evidence_items.summary: Introduction and Definition: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare refers to computational systems that help with analyzing, interpreting, and applying health data in clinical practice, public health practice, research, and administration. The World Health Organization (WHO) defines AI as "the capability of algorithms integrated into systems and tools to learn from data". Early clinical decision support systems, such as MYCIN in the 1970s, demonstrated how computers could be helpful in medical reasoning. Body: Machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal models, and generative AI all fall under AI in healthcare. Image interpretation, clinical documentation, risk prediction, triage, drug discovery, patient monitoring, public health surveillance, and personalized treatment plans represent some of the applications of artificial intelligence in the field. For the technology to be clinically effective, it must be validated, incorporated into clinical workflows, and shown to produce meaningful outcomes. FDA-authorized AI-enabled medical devices are becoming more common in clinical practice, particularly in imaging specialties. Multimodal biomedical AI, foundation models, and large language models that could process text, images, laboratory results, and other health data are the focus of current research. AI tools undergoing research, devices authorized for clinical use, and technologies demonstrated to improve patient outcomes represent distinct stages of development and evaluation. Conclusion: Artificial intelligence may improve healthcare efficiency, clinical decision support, research productivity, and access to care. However, clinical benefits depend on rigorous evaluation and appropriate implementation. Potential risks include algorithmic bias, patient privacy concerns, unreliable outputs, and limited transparency. Human oversight and continued monitoring remain important for responsible implementation.

evidence_items.summary: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) is an emerging technology in orthodontics that facilitates the identification and assessment of dental abnormalities through automated image analysis. Its application may support early recognition of malocclusion and preventive orthodontic care. Objectives: To evaluate the role of artificial intelligence in the early identification of orthodontic abnormalities and assess its diagnostic performance compared with clinical orthodontic examination. Study Design & Setting: Descriptive cross-sectional study conducted at the Department of Orthodontics, Shahida Islam Dental College, Lodhran from March 2026 to September 2026. Methodology: A total of 150 patients aged 6–18 years were included using a non-probability consecutive sampling technique. Demographic information and orthodontic findings were recorded through clinical examination and standardized intraoral photographs. Dental photographs were analysed using an AI-based assessment system, and its findings were compared with clinical diagnoses established by an experienced orthodontist. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, diagnostic accuracy, and Cohen's kappa coefficient were calculated. Results: The mean age of participants was 11.8 ± 3.4 years, with males comprising 52.0% of the sample. Dental crowding was the most frequent orthodontic abnormality (42.0%), followed by increased overjet (26.0%). Artificial intelligence identified abnormalities in 77.3% of participants. The diagnostic assessment demonstrated a sensitivity of 89.0%, specificity of 65.6%, positive predictive value of 90.5%, negative predictive value of 61.8%, and overall accuracy of 84.0%. Agreement between AI assessment and clinical examination was 84.0%, with a reported Cohen's kappa coefficient of 0.59. Conclusion: Artificial intelligence demonstrated promising performance in identifying orthodontic abnormalities and may support early orthodontic screening.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Orthodontic Prevention

evidence_items.summary: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for acute cervical spine fracture (CSFx) detection, but its performance across diverse computed tomography (CT) protocols in unselected emergency workflows requires validation. This study evaluated an AI application on dedicated non-contrast cervical spine CTs and conducted a ‘stress test’ on contrast-enhanced whole-body trauma CTs. Methods: This retrospective study included 724 consecutive adults undergoing cervical spine or whole-body CT at a Level I trauma center (November 2023–February 2025). Disagreements with retrospective review defaulted to the original senior-validated clinical report, reflecting agreement with routine practice rather than an independent expert consensus. Results: Overall, 79/724 patients had acute CSFx (10.9% prevalence), including 54/627 (8.6%) imaged for acute initial trauma. On non-contrast CTs (n = 298), the AI achieved 88.0% sensitivity (95% CI: 76.2–94.4), 88.3% specificity, 60.3% positive predictive value (PPV), and 97.3% negative predictive value (NPV); in the acute-initial-trauma non-contrast subgroup (n = 204), sensitivity was 80.0% (20/25; 95% CI: 60.9–91.1). On contrast-enhanced CTs (n = 426), sensitivity was 86.2%, whereas specificity was lower (75.1%), associated with arterial opacification artifacts and protocol-group differences. Exact vertebral level localization was achieved in 60/69 (87.0%) detected positive examinations and 60/79 (75.9%) fracture-positive examinations. Conclusions: Evaluated for agreement with routine senior-validated clinical reports, the AI showed high sensitivity and NPV in an unselected cohort, suggesting potential triage utility, though acute-initial-trauma non-contrast sensitivity was lower (80.0%) and workflow impact remains unmeasured. Arterial-phase acquisitions were associated with higher false-positive rates, warranting protocol-aware interpretation.
evidence_items.title: Real-World Clinical Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Application for Acute Cervical Spine Fracture Detection on CT
